Container.Name: sftp
Container.Overview: A hardened OpenSSH SFTP server with chroot jails and fail2ban, in one container. Each account is jailed in its home directory, fail2ban bans password guessers, and the /config folder holds everything, applied again on every start.[br][br]The admin web UI is on, over HTTPS on port 8443. On first start the container's log prints a setup link for the first admin that works once, for one hour: open it with this server's address and the web UI port, then choose a name and a password. The web UI adds and changes accounts, keys, permissions, groups, settings, bans and country rules, and changes apply at once. Change the server's settings there rather than adding variables here: a variable set here wins over the Settings page, even when it is empty.[br][br]Give an account a folder with another path: a share on the host, mounted in the container at /home/NAME/FOLDER, where NAME is the account's name. The file browser for account holders stays off until File browser is true.

Config.Name: SFTP port
Config.Description: The port SFTP clients connect to. Unraid's own SSH server already listens on 22.

Config.Name: Admin web UI port
Config.Description: The admin web UI, over HTTPS.

Config.Name: File browser port
Config.Description: The file browser, over HTTPS, when File browser is true.

Config.Name: Config
Config.Description: Accounts, keys, settings, logs and the web UI's data.

Config.Name: Admin web UI
Config.Description: true runs the admin web UI.

Config.Name: File browser
Config.Description: true runs the file browser for accounts given the web option. It needs the admin web UI.

Config.Name: Trusted networks
Config.Description: Networks, such as 192.168.1.0/24, from which admins and file browser users sign in without a two-factor code, and which the country rules always let in.

Config.Name: Trusted proxies
Config.Description: Reverse proxies allowed to connect in plain HTTP and to send X-Forwarded-For.

Config.Name: Plain HTTP
Config.Description: true serves plain HTTP, for a reverse proxy. It needs Trusted proxies.
